cases.name: Christa Worthington
cases.about: Christa was a United States fashion writer who worked for Women's Wear Daily, Cosmopolitan, ELLE, Harper's Bazaar, and The New York Times. She was also a co-author of several books on fashion.
cases.narrative: On 1/06/2002, her body was found by a neighbor and former boyfriend, Tim Arnold, on the floor of her home with her two-year-old daughter, Ava, clinging to her. Ava was trying to nurse from her mother. Police believe the little girl had spent 24 to 36 hours in the house with her mother lying on the floor, fatally stabbed.

cases.name: Susan Stolberg Howe
cases.about:
She was the head of the Truro Historical Society. 

Her obituary said, "She was born in Baltimore, MD in 1952 along with her twin sister Carol Stolberg. Susan graduated from Syracuse University and received a degree in Psychology. She went on to obtain a Master’s degree from Boston University as a Rehabilitation Counselor. Susan raised her children in Belmont MA and spent many summers in Truro, MA before becoming a fulltime resident. Prior to raising her family she worked for many years at Tufts, New England Medical Center.

She was passionate about music, playing the guitar and piano. Susan sang songs with preschoolers, taught guitar lessons, and shared her love of music with her children. She loved attending the opera with her daughter, Jenna, and their friend Katy. In Truro she spent time in her garden and taking pictures of people and beautiful landscapes. When elsewhere, she loved to travel with friends and had a specific love of Paris.

Susan became involved in the community working as a disabilities advocate and the President of the Truro Historical Society. Living in Truro, she immediately felt welcomed, and became a huge presence advocating for the community she loved. Susan helped to renovate a Truro playground and make it accessible to people of all abilities. She pushed for repairs at the museum honoring Truro’s history. She encouraged residents and businesses to display blue lights to raise awareness about autism. Susan believed Truro should remain rural.

Susan was frequently found walking her dog, Sprite, along Longnook and Corn Hill beaches. She was loved by all and spent many happy days sharing her life in Truro with friends and family. She will be greatly missed by all of the people who loved her."
